statement: Fix k ≥ 3, B > 0, and 0 < δ < 1/2. Suppose that there are constants 0 < a ≤ A < B and numbers ηn ≥ 0 tending to zero such that, for all sufficiently large n, a ≤ en ≤ A, P (︁ |Tn − µn| ≥ n1−δ)︁ ≤ ηn. (B.2) Then there is a finite constant K ≥ 0 such that, for all sufficiently large n = min{n1, n2}, with no restriction on n1/n2, en1+n2 ≥ min{en1 , en2 } − Kn−δ , (B.3) and, for all sufficiently large n, en+1 ≥ en − Kn−δ . (B.4) Moreover en converges to a number α ∈ [a, A], and Pn(⌊cn⌋) −→ {︄ 1, 0 ≤ c < α, 0, c > α. (B.5) 23 For every sufficiently large s and every N ≥ s2, one has the one-sided estimate eN ≥ es − K(1 + Bδ)s−δ , Bδ = (3/2)δ 1 − (2/3)δ . (B.6)
